This exuberantly silly musical adaptation of the Nickelodeon cartoon series is a candy-colored rush of joy that somehow manages to be both faithfully nonsensical and surprisingly touching.

The wonders of Tina Landau’s production pour from the stage in a ravishing stream of color and invention that sucks you into its merry, silly currents.

With its soaring music, hilarious performances, tug-at-the-heartstrings story, and jaw-dropping design, SpongeBob SquarePants, the musical has quickly cemented itself as one of my favorite musicals I’ve ever seen.
"Spongebob Squarepants: The Musical" is one of the best musicals on Broadway right now, and is certainly the best musical of the season.
For all that the multi-colored SpongeBob musical cavalcade is a party for the eyes and ears, it is also political—radical even.
Theatrical staging is a continuous giddy delight.
Just a simple Sponge? "SpongeBob," at the Palace Theatre, is simply a pleasure.
"In the end, SpongeBob succeeds because [Tina] Landau and [David] Zinn make even the most complicated musical staging look and feel like child’s play.

Now the grand playhouse has been transformed into a brightly festive Bikini Bottom, underwater home of that bubbly, lovable cartoon character and cultural phenomenon SpongeBob SquarePants, making his Broadway debut in a self-titled musical that’s an absolute delight.
Well, hats off to director Tina Landau and her gifted company for being able to ride the wave so entertainingly.
Holiday cheer has arrived — in the form of 'nautical nonsense.'
For kids and kids at heart, this is a sweet, watery treat.

Overall, it's an entertaining, if overstuffed and a bit too experimental, homage to the long-running cartoon — though audience members over the age of 11 may leave the theater with a touch of seasickness.
A theatergoer who isn’t seven years old or stoned or an unusually empathetic parent may secretly wish before the 150 minutes are up that Humongous will destroy Bikini Bottom soon.
Otherwise, it’s a tame evening for those who enter the Palace gates without a preexisting affinity for SpongeBob SquarePants.
It’s all admirably imaginative.

cn.t: Critics largely embrace this splashy, visually dazzling spectacle, with Ethan Slater's star-making performance earning near-universal praise. Some find it overstuffed, but its infectious energy and imaginative staging win most over.

vs.sum: Spectacularly renovated in a $100M+ project that literally raised the theater 30 feet. The restoration preserved its opulent 1913 interior while upgrading acoustics, seating comfort, and best-in-class restrooms on every level — widely considered the best facilities on Broadway.

acc.note: Elevator to all levels. Wheelchair, aisle transfer, and companion seating on all levels.
